notice: These are bounded non-production model blueprints. Numeric envelopes are conservative engineering caps, not effect sizes copied from the studies.

minor.purpose: Narrow, weak, indirect, or incompletely verified signals.

moderate.purpose: Direct feeding or catchability direction with meaningful setting or transfer uncertainty.

strong-conservative.purpose: Direct and comparatively strong evidence, still capped pending validation.

severe-stress.purpose: Only for an exact severe physiological condition; never an ordinary-weather penalty.

rules.inputContract: Local solar-relative time and selected date.

validRange.season: late summer through early autumn; strongest source support is September-October
validRange.solarWindow: sunset through night, with strongest support during the first 90 minutes after sunset

rules.proposedResponse: Use a smooth, moderate post-sunset increase and a modest daylight decrease; attenuate outside the source season and in non-estuarine waters.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral when local solar time cannot be calculated.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Use one light/diel factor; do not stack sunset, clock time, cloud, and generic nocturnal weights.

rules.inputContract: Local solar-relative time and selected date.

validRange.observedClockWindows: verified July study: primary peak 16:00-20:00, minor increase 04:00-08:00, lowest feeding 08:00-16:00, and a sharp decrease 00:00-04:00

rules.proposedResponse: Allow only a minor dawn increase and a larger but still minor late-day increase in summer, expressed relative to local solar time rather than assuming the New York clock intervals transfer exactly.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral outside summer or when local solar time cannot be calculated.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Do not add this to a generic crepuscular multiplier.
validationRequirements: verified 16:00-20:00 primary and 04:00-08:00 secondary peak ordering

rules.evidenceClass: controlled maximum-ration experiment using Virginia tidal-river fish
rules.inputContract: Observed or modeled water temperature in degrees C with provenance and uncertainty.

validRange.anchors: 5 C lower consumption; 15 C and 25 C statistically similar

rules.proposedResponse: Reduce the existing thermal suitability toward 5 C, reach neutral by 15 C, and add no bonus from 15-25 C.
rules.missingBehavior: Fall back to the documented seasonal prior when water temperature is unavailable.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Modify the existing thermal curve; never multiply a separate cold penalty by it.

rules.inputContract: Observed or modeled water temperature plus a sustained-temperature indicator.

validRange.exposure: sustained acclimation, not an acute warm afternoon

rules.proposedResponse: Treat 18 C as neutral and apply a smoothly increasing, capped penalty approaching 25 C only after sustained warm exposure.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral when temperature history is unavailable.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Use this to shape the warm side of the thermal factor; do not stack it with a generic heat penalty.

rules.inputContract: Local solar-relative time, selected date, and very-cold-water state.
rules.proposedResponse: Apply only a minor nighttime increase under comparable winter water temperatures; otherwise retain the baseline diel profile.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral if water temperature is unavailable or outside the winter study context.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Replace, rather than stack with, the generic nocturnal multiplier.

rules.evidenceClass: winter feeding experiment plus confounded field comparison
rules.inputContract: Observed or modeled water temperature in degrees C.

validRange.anchors: feeding observed at 3 C; stronger modeled predation by 4.5 C; one field comparison reported no feeding near 2 C

rules.proposedResponse: Keep expected feeding nonzero at 3 C, apply a stronger capped penalty near 2 C, and recover toward 4.5 C without claiming a universal threshold.
rules.missingBehavior: Use the seasonal prior when water temperature is unavailable.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: This is the cold tail of the thermal factor, not an additional winter penalty.

rules.evidenceClass: reservoir stomach chronology plus winter feeding experiment
rules.inputContract: Observed or modeled water temperature and recent thermal history.

validRange.anchors: continued feeding at 7 C; progressively higher intake across <=10, 10.1-15.6, and 15.7-21.1 C

rules.proposedResponse: Represent progressive cold-season suppression without cessation; use temperature rather than calendar month as the main driver.
rules.missingBehavior: Fall back to the monthly seasonal prior.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Blend this into the single seasonal-thermal factor; do not multiply monthly winter and cold-water penalties.

rules.inputContract: Water-temperature change over the preceding 24-48 hours in degrees C.

validRange.trend: cooling versus stable or warming winter conditions

rules.proposedResponse: Apply a minor penalty on cooling days in the tested cold-water range; stable and warming conditions receive no bonus above neutral.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral without at least 24 hours of comparable water-temperature history.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Cap the combined level-and-trend thermal contribution; do not use air-pressure or weather-front labels as substitutes.

rules.inputContract: Observed or modeled water temperature plus recent heat-exposure history.
rules.proposedResponse: Apply no separate bonus at 27-31 C; increase the existing high-temperature penalty only as sustained conditions enter 31-35 C.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral beyond the ordinary thermal factor when heat history is unavailable.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Replace the high-temperature tail of the thermal curve and ignore stress-related tank activity as positive catchability.

rules.inputContract: Observed or modeled water temperature in degrees C.

validRange.anchors: very low at 6 C, higher by 14 C, highest highlighted treatment at 28 C, lower at 34 C

rules.proposedResponse: Fit a conservative shape through the four observed anchors without treating 28 C as a universal field optimum or extrapolating outside 6-34 C.
rules.missingBehavior: Fall back to seasonal activity when water temperature is unavailable.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Replace the existing thermal response; do not stack cold and warm carp rules separately.

rules.inputContract: Local solar-relative time and selected date.
rules.proposedResponse: Apply a minor early-evening increase and modest morning decrease in summer, expressed relative to local sunset rather than fixed clock time.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral outside summer or without local solar time.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Do not stack with a generic crepuscular profile.

rules.inputContract: Local solar-relative time and selected date.

validRange.timing: a distinct peak is confirmed; the claimed late-day placement requires full-text sign-off

rules.proposedResponse: Remain neutral unless the primary full text or author-supplied material establishes the exact peak interval; the supplied late-day interpretation is not accepted as verified evidence.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral before full-text peak-timing review and outside summer.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Do not stack with a generic diel pattern.
validationRequirements: full-text peak interval required before activation

rules.inputContract: Observed or modeled water temperature in degrees C.

validRange.anchors: rare feeding below 15 C, most stopped at 11 C, none observed at 7 C or lower

rules.proposedResponse: Shape the existing cold-water tail around the observed anchors while retaining a small nonzero field possibility and avoiding extrapolation below 3 C.
rules.missingBehavior: Use the seasonal prior when water temperature is unavailable.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: This replaces the low-temperature tail; it is not an additional winter multiplier.

rules.inputContract: Rolling estimated or observed water-temperature history, not a single hot-hour reading.
rules.proposedResponse: Apply a severe-heat penalty only as multi-day exposure approaches 35 C; the study does not define the onset temperature, so ordinary hot days remain governed by the baseline thermal curve.
rules.missingBehavior: No additional penalty without rolling water-temperature history.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Replace the extreme upper tail and do not stack with generic heat, seasonal summer, or low-oxygen penalties without an interaction model.

rules.inputContract: Forecast surface solar radiation or a solar-relative low-light classification for lake/reservoir locations.
rules.proposedResponse: Apply a small decrease from very low toward high radiation; do not reproduce the study probability difference directly as BiteMap points.
rules.missingBehavior: Use solar-relative light at reduced confidence, otherwise neutral.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Cloud, radiation, and diel period feed one latent light factor and cannot stack.

rules.evidenceClass: local tidal-river field feeding and movement study
rules.inputContract: Local solar-relative time and selected date.

validRange.waterbody: tidal Potomac and comparable tidal river habitat

rules.proposedResponse: Apply a bounded morning/daylight increase and overnight decrease in May-June; strongly attenuate outside the source season or tidal setting.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral without local solar time or location scope.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Use one diel/tide joint cap so daylight and outgoing tide cannot independently reach full strength.

rules.inputContract: Forecast or computed tidal stage for the spot and selected hour.

validRange.waterbody: tidal Potomac and comparable tidal water

rules.proposedResponse: Apply a minor outgoing-tide increase only where a trustworthy tidal prediction exists; other stages remain neutral rather than penalized.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral on non-tidal waters or without a tidal prediction.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Cap the combined snakehead diel and tide response because time of day and tide covaried in the study.

rules.inputContract: Observed turbidity in NTU, or FNU only when the provider documents comparable optics; never suspended sediment mass.
rules.proposedResponse: Apply a modest decreasing response within 0-40 NTU and clamp outside the range; do not claim that every amount of stained water is harmful in the field.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral when representative turbidity is unavailable or the unit is not comparable.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Do not stack turbidity with rainfall or flow as separate visibility penalties.

rules.inputContract: Representative dissolved oxygen in mg/L and water temperature in degrees C.
rules.proposedResponse: Use a moderate penalty near 2 mg/L, a smaller penalty near 4 mg/L, and neutral at adequate oxygen; add no oxygen bonus above the tested adequate condition.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral with reduced confidence when representative dissolved oxygen is unavailable.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Replace the generic striped-bass oxygen term and cap any warm-water interaction rather than multiplying two full penalties.

rules.inputContract: Local solar-relative period and optionally forecast surface solar radiation for lake/reservoir locations.
rules.proposedResponse: Apply bounded dawn and dusk increases relative to day, with radiation as an alternate continuous representation rather than an additional factor.
rules.missingBehavior: Use solar-relative period alone when radiation is missing; otherwise neutral.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Dawn/dusk, cloud, and solar radiation are one latent light signal and cannot stack.

rules.inputContract: Observed or modeled water temperature in degrees C.
rules.proposedResponse: Use a broad intermediate-temperature plateau with lower suitability at 19 and 28 C; do not treat 25 C as a precise adult field optimum.
rules.missingBehavior: Fall back to the seasonal prior when water temperature is unavailable.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Replace the existing thermal response and do not add a second warm or cool penalty.
validationRequirements: broad plateau rather than point optimum

rules.inputContract: Local solar-relative time and selected date.

validRange.solarWindow: feeding rises through daylight, peaks late evening, and declines after sunset

rules.proposedResponse: Use a modest daylight ramp toward late evening and decline after sunset; attenuate in turbid water and outside summer.
rules.missingBehavior: Neutral without local solar time; use reduced confidence when clarity is unknown.
rules.doubleCountingGuard: Use one diel/light factor and do not stack a separate dusk or cloud modifier.
